title: CrossBit: Bitwise Computing in NAND Flash Memory with Inter-Bitline Data Communication
problem: Existing in-flash processing (IFP) architectures can only perform bitwise operations on data sensed within the same bitline, preventing computation involving data from different bitlines. This restriction makes prior IFP designs unable to implement error correction codes (ECC) or efficiently process database query operations that require inter-bitline data interactions.
motivation: NAND flash memory's high capacity and low cost make it attractive for near-data processing of data-intensive workloads, but the limited intra-bitline-only operation support severely restricts the computational scope and forces continued use of less dense SLC cells without reliable in-flash ECC.
method: CrossBit adds communication pathways to NAND flash memory so different bitlines (columns of storage cells) can exchange data during in-flash computation. Normally, flash can only operate on data within a single bitline, but these pathways break that barrier. This enables error correction (ECC) to work directly on multi-level cells (MLC, which store multiple bits per cell), and it accelerates database operations like filtering and joins that need to combine data from multiple bitlines.
key_novelty: CrossBit is the first in-flash processor to enable data from different bitlines to interact during computation, making it possible to run error correction on multi-level cells and a wider range of database operations entirely within the flash chip.
contributions: An IFP architecture (CrossBit) supporting both intra-bitline and inter-bitline bulk bitwise operations with minimal additional circuitry
In-flash ECC (IF-ECC) implementation that enables reliable MLC IFP, achieving 1.8x bit density improvement over prior SLC-only IFP
Demonstration that CrossBit accelerates fundamental database queries (selection, joins) with 2.1x speedup and 2.5x energy efficiency over state-of-the-art IFP
End-to-end evaluation on the Star Schema Benchmark showing 1.7x speedup over prior IFP

metrics.speedup: 2.1x over SOTA IFP for database queries; 1.7x on Star Schema Benchmark end-to-end
metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 2.5x energy efficiency improvement over SOTA IFP
metrics.other: 1.8x bit density increase using MLC vs SLC in prior IFP

limitations: Evaluation is limited to database query workloads; applicability to other data-intensive domains (e.g., ML inference) is not quantitatively assessed.
primary_theme: inter-bitline in-flash computation for databases and MLC ECC
